Wait, the runner.py uses `-I` flag with check.py? Actually check.py invokes `runner.py` with `-I -B`. Hmm, `-I` implies isolated mode which ignores PYTHONPATH etc. Then runner execs `sys.executable, ['-B', sys.argv[1]]` — but that doesn't include `-I`. OK.

Note: `-I` means `sys.path` won't include the script dir... actually with `-I`, the script's directory is still prepended? `-I` implies `-E -s`: ignore PYTHON* env vars, and don't prepend user site-packages. In Python 3.11, `-I` doesn't prevent adding the script's directory to sys.path. Actually `-I` = "-E -s -P"? No: `-P` doesn't prepend. From docs: "-I: Run Python in isolated mode. This also implies -E, -P and -s options." In 3.11, -I implies -E, -P and -s. So sys.path[0] containing the script directory is NOT added. Then runner.py execs with just `-B`, so sys.path[0] will be the dir of main.py (which after chdir is the project dir; sys.argv[1] is the absolute path of candidate main.py). Good.
